prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: The two parts answer my test of whether chemistry changed what researchers and clinicians can actually do. C-N coupling is the mature, mechanistically grounded enabling reaction that three of my colleagues ranked first; ligand design turned a harsh, narrow transformation into a routine one used daily in drug discovery and materials synthesis, and it completes the logic of the 2010 cross-coupling prize for a bond type it left out. Base editing is a rational molecular-design achievement, engineered deaminase-Cas fusions that perform defined single-nucleotide chemistry without double-strand breaks, now reproduced across many labs and in patients. Two achievements from different corners of chemistry, one a synthetic method and one a biomolecular tool, make a balanced prize, and the union of three people fits the rules.
statement.case_against: Crediting only Liu for B004 leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, whose first-author work on the cytosine and adenine editors was decisive, and the Nishida/Kondo Target-AID line is independent. A committee that wants to honor the inventors rather than the laboratory head may find this unsatisfying. Base editing also follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely and clinical outcome data are still emerging, so it may be judged slightly early or derivative. For B052, Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work leaves a precursor-credit question, and Hartwig's presence on the C-H functionalization entry means the same people could be recognized under several candidates.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a clear game-changer that extends the 2010 cross-coupling logic to a new bond type, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the natural independent pair and Kosugi as a precursor.
responses.response: I agree and have moved B052 from outside my opening top four into my preferred configuration. Your point about ligand design and mechanism leading to capability is the strongest argument for it, and I accept that Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry is a precursor and not the general method. I would not let this be the whole prize, though, because you also ranked base editing third and I think the pair of achievements is stronger than either alone.

responses.point: C-N coupling is among the most used bond-forming methods in drug discovery and recognition is overdue, since the 2010 prize covered only C-C coupling. Somfai also ranked photoredox catalysis and C-H functionalization next.
responses.response: The overdue argument persuades me and it is why B052 now anchors my configuration. I disagree mildly that photoredox is the better second part: MacMillan's 2021 prize makes the trio awkward, and the three-name limit forces exclusions from an already crowded field. I place more weight on a second part that opens a new capability in biomedicine, which is where base editing sits.

responses.point: Liquid-liquid phase separation is a physical-chemical idea of unusual generality, with the 2009 P-granule work as the identifiable discovery and Hyman and Brangwynne as the cleanest pair.
responses.response: I respect this as a conceptual contribution and kept B002 as an alternative, but I have a serious reservation. The in vivo claims still depend heavily on overexpression and imaging, and the attribution is not settled with Rosen, Pappu and Mittag making independent foundational contributions. A prize whose credited pair omits the multivalency and sequence-grammar framework risks recognizing a phenomenon more than the chemistry. I would favor B002 once the physiological-relevance debate narrows.

responses.point: Base editing is a clean chemical-mechanism story that avoids break-driven repair, with Liu's laboratory conceiving both editor classes and Komor and Gaudelli leading the cytosine and adenine editors. A fair prize could be built around them.
responses.response: I share your view of the science and ranked B004 first. My only qualification is arithmetic: if B052 is also awarded, the three-person limit leaves one seat for B004, and I would credit Liu alone and acknowledge Komor and Gaudelli in the discussion. If the committee prefers all three inventors on a single-part prize, I would rather see B004 as the sole achievement than drop Komor or Gaudelli arbitrarily.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly problem solved by design, with Cullis and Hope as the formulation pioneers, and her view of B045 follows from the physical chemistry of pH-dependent charge and nanostructure.
responses.response: This is close to my own field of interest and I agree about the design logic, but I do not think B045 is ready for this year's top slot. Credit spreads across Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and the 2023 Medicine prize already honored the nucleoside-modification half of the mRNA story. I would hold it for later.

uncertainties: Whether Liu alone is an acceptable credit for base editing or whether Komor and Gaudelli must be named, which would force a single-part prize
How much weight the committee gives Kosugi's precursor work in C-N coupling
Whether base editing is too close to the 2020 CRISPR prize and too early on clinical outcomes
Whether targeted protein degradation will gain an approved drug soon enough to overtake base editing as the biomedical choice
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My Linkoping biosensor and peptide work has no direct connection to any shortlisted candidate, and my postdoc mentors Stevens and Boey are not credited on the shortlist.
